claim: Offline planning steps on a learned model speed learning after a new fact; in a tiny maze n=5 reached near-optimal in about 5 episodes vs about 25 for n=0 (Sutton and Barto). Prioritised ordering cuts it further.
agent_test: Replay stored traces between tasks at fixed token budget; compare 0, few, many replay passes on a held-out repeated-task set.

claim: Plain Dyna-Q cannot discover a new shortcut because its model says none exists; an exploration bonus (Dyna-Q+) or re-testing stale model parts is needed.
agent_test: Change a task fact after library build; check whether the update step re-tests old stale subgoals vs only replaying successes. a02, a26 and b06 trace to the Sutton and Barto book; b29 unverified.

claim: Prioritised replay (by expected value or prediction error) beats uniform replay: 41 of 49 Atari games (Schaul), fewer observations to 98% optimal (Moore and Atkeson 94k vs 155k-240k in 2627-state mazes), and a normative EVB = Gain x Need account (Mattar and Daw). Gap search: Moore and Atkeson Table 2 re-read as image and confirmed (stochastic 2627-state: PriSweep 94,000, Dyna-opt 155,000, Dyna-PI+ 240,000); exceptions on small mazes (15-state stochastic: 600 vs 400; one small problem Dyna-PI+ 252 vs PriSweep 472). Order matters most when the state space is large and the backup budget small.
agent_test: Rank stored traces for replay by surprise (failed predictions) times likely reuse; compare to random order at equal tokens.

claim: Humans revalue after a reward change more than after a transition change, both above control (exp1 n=58: .520/.450/.031; exp2 n=88: .66/.47/.50/.08). Re-opened and confirmed for exp2 and the exp1 t-tests.
agent_test: Test the agent on reward-change vs transition-change updates to the same task knowledge; expect transition changes to be harder. One lab, two experiments, so counted as one source; internal replication only.

claim: The human data are best fit by a hybrid SR-MB model; the label 'SR-Dyna fit human revaluation best' comes from the 2020 review and simulations, not from fitting SR-Dyna to the 2017 human data. Independent 2025 data (Kahn and Daw, n=100) also show a mix of SR and model-based weights (0.866 vs 0.88), shifting to SR when futures are predictable.
agent_test: None directly; treat the label as unproven when citing.

claim: Dyna-Q with too little replay degrades to model-free and fails all three revaluation tests; SR-Dyna with too little replay still passes reward revaluation. Simulation result.
agent_test: Analogy only: cheap cached summaries (SR-like) survive low replay budgets, full re-derivation does not. Test: low vs high replay budget with summary vs full-trace storage.

claim: Replay during rest in humans is linked to later replanning after revaluation (fMRI n=24, rho .54 vs -.13; difference p=.023), but the claim that the link is stronger under reward noise is not supported by the primary data (interaction p=.34). Gap search: an independent lab (Zhang et al. 2026, n=119+119 aged 7 to 23, adapted task) found reward revaluation drove replanning with or without a 60 s rest; the rest effect was not significant (p=.13, trend the wrong way). Not a direct replication, but no outside support for a rest-replay benefit.
agent_test: Check whether replay volume after a surprise predicts a later plan change in the agent; do not tune on a variance moderator.

claim: Human MEG rest replay follows learned structure rather than experienced order and transfers to unseen objects (n=21, n=22).
agent_test: Test whether offline restructuring of traces by abstract rule (not by order seen) improves transfer to new surface content.

claim: Replay in rats is not only for planning: it can reflect past experience and remote locations, and did not predict the next choice in Gillespie et al. (4 rats); it may serve memory maintenance.
agent_test: Do not assume replay targets the next task; include replay of old, unvisited items in the library update.

claim: Hippocampal damage impairs model-based planning in humans (19 patients vs 19 controls).
agent_test: None.

claim: In deep RL, one-step Dyna with a learned model gives little benefit over simply more updates on real data; value updates from simulated states can mislead (hallucinated value); short branched rollouts from real states are safer.
agent_test: Use short simulations branched from real stored cases; compare with re-reading stored cases the same number of times.

claim: Offline reasoning before the question arrives cuts test-time compute about 5x at equal accuracy and adds up to +13% (GSM) / +18% (AIME); cost per query falls 2.5x with related queries; helps most when the question is predictable from the context; not worth it with few queries. Re-opened and confirmed (abstract and text). Gap search: the control is equal TEST-time tokens (pass@k at the same test budget); no comparison at equal total tokens including sleep-time was found, and no replication by another group.
agent_test: Run a sleep-time pass on stored task context; compare accuracy per total tokens in single-query vs multi-query settings.

claim: In LLM agents, simulating next states before acting helps: WebDreamer GPT-4o VWA 17.6 to 23.6 (+34.1% rel), 4-5x faster than real tree search (26.2). Re-opened and confirmed. Prompted rollouts also help untrained models a little (Dyna-Mind).
agent_test: Prompted lookahead with a model-written outcome guess vs reactive, equal tokens.

claim: Quality of the model's own simulation matters: GPT-4 as text-world simulator is at most 59.9% accurate on non-trivial state changes; world-model accuracy correlates with success (r >= 0.32 in Dyna-Think, confirmed; Dyna-Mind r up to .96 for R1 on Sokoban, falling after RL). Dyna-Mind (same group) adds across-model points: ALFWorld sim score 0.18/0.35/0.36 goes with success 35.4/55.2/62.5 vs 87.7 at exact simulation; Sokoban 0.21/0.54/0.93 with 25.8/57.0/96.6. No break-even threshold study found.
agent_test: Score the agent's predicted outcomes against real tool results; gate use of simulated lookahead on a measured hit rate.

claim: Naive Dyna with a separately trained world model does not reliably help LLM agents: OSWorld vanilla Dyna avg 23.2 vs RFT 23.2 (no gain), WindowsAgentArena 20.9 vs 28.4 (hurt); training the model to simulate inside its own reasoning (DDT) helped (26.6; 34.9). Re-opened Table 3.
agent_test: Compare a separate simulator call vs in-thread simulation at equal tokens. b22 mislabels the 24.1 figure (see critique).

claim: Synthetic experience from an LLM world model with a replay buffer can partly replace real interaction. DreamGym Table 1 (read as image; order WebShop, ALFWorld, WebArena; each Llama-3.2-3B, Llama-3.1-8B, Qwen-2.5-7B). GRPO 80K real vs DreamGym 0 real: WebShop 62.1/65.0/66.1 vs 59.3/63.9/68.3; ALFWorld 65.3/70.9/79.8 vs 62.1/66.3/71.0; WebArena 7.3/6.1/6.1 vs 13.3/9.1/12.7. Adding 5K real after synthetic (S2R) beats 80K real in most cells (e.g. WebShop Llama-8B 75.0). Earlier ablation numbers (3 to 6 point drops) were confirmed in the prior pass.
agent_test: Training-based; not directly testable without training. Column mapping now fixed (see evidence d09). Lesson: simulated experience is a partial substitute; ALFWorld Qwen lost 8.8 points to real GRPO.

claim: Offline induction of reusable routines from past successes into memory improves web agents: Agent Workflow Memory WebArena 35.5 vs 23.5 (+12.0 points, +51.1% rel). Re-opened and confirmed. Gap search: on Mind2Web the offline-from-training and online-self-induced versions are close in-task (Step SR 45.1 vs 43.6) and online pulls ahead as the train-test gap grows (cross-domain 32.6 vs 35.5); whole-task SR stays under 5 percent.
agent_test: Induce workflows from solved items offline and retrieve them; compare with no memory at equal tokens.

claim: Text reflection on failures and stored skill or insight libraries improve LLM agents across trials (Reflexion, ExpeL, Generative Agents, Voyager). Numbers are from the papers' own benchmarks; not re-opened here.
agent_test: Compare reflection-memory against fresh attempt at equal tokens, on repeated item families.

claim: Frontier LLMs show weak cognitive-map planning and no emergent revaluation: GPT-4 CogEval 1-step .99, 3-step .55, transition revaluation .60, detour .55, shortcut .56 (re-opened and confirmed); chain-of-thought and BFS/DFS prompts help little.
agent_test: Run the human revaluation tasks on our scaffolded agent with and without a replay step.

claim: Bigger or longer replay can hurt: large buffers hurt (Zhang and Sutton), benefits of capacity differ by algorithm (Fedus).
agent_test: Cap library size; test newest-first inclusion against pure random replay.

claim: Policy reuse via successor features plus GPI explained human choice better than model-based or model-free in 3 of 4 experiments (N=132, 96, 113, 303).
agent_test: Test reuse of stored sub-policies for a new goal vs re-planning.

claim: A write gate beats storing everything: in LLM agent memories, add-all of self-generated experience lowers accuracy 3 to 12 points below a fixed small memory, while strict outcome-checked addition gains 3 to 22 points (Xiong 2025, four agents, GPT-4o-mini). ReMe (selective vs full add +3.50 Avg@4) and ACE (feedback needed) agree. Deletion by retrieval count and utility helps only with a good evaluator.
agent_test: Gate every library write on a checked outcome; log retrieval count and outcome per entry; test add-all vs gated at equal tokens.

claim: Recency is as good as a learned retention score when the library is clean (FIFO-K50 190/200 vs 190/200 on ALFWorld, gpt-5-mini); outcome-aware scoring pays off only under polluted writes (Precision@5 3.8% FIFO vs 16.6% scored with 75% distractors). Learned case selection beats similarity by under 1 point (Memento 85.44 vs 84.85). No test of surprise-versus-need priority on an LLM library exists.
agent_test: Start with recency plus outcome gate; test reuse-weighted priority only after measuring pollution.

claim: Corrupted memory updates have a dose-response: 1 bad update in 5 or fewer is tolerated, every-step corruption drops accuracy below base (FiNER 70.7 base; every step 66.7; every 5 steps 76.1; none 78.3). One locally correct but non-transferable case can become an over-general rule (OEP, ASR above 50%).
agent_test: Inject known-wrong entries at 5 to 20 percent into a library and measure the accuracy loss before trusting simulated updates.

claim: Library staleness is measured only indirectly: workflows induced offline from a different distribution trail those induced online on the live distribution by 0.2 to 2.9 Step SR points on Mind2Web (cross-website 33.7 vs 33.9; cross-domain 32.6 vs 35.5). No LLM study tests explicit stale-subgoal detection after a task change (Dyna-Q+ analogue).
agent_test: After a task change, compare a library with scheduled re-test of old entries to one without.

claim: Across models, simulation accuracy rises with success (ALFWorld sim 0.18/0.35/0.36/1.00 with success 35.4/55.2/62.5/87.7), but no study varies simulation accuracy at fixed model to find a break-even hit rate for lookahead over reactive acting.
agent_test: Vary simulator accuracy at fixed model (noisy oracle) and find the point where lookahead stops beating reactive.

claim: No LLM study compares an offline replay pass with a fresh attempt at equal total tokens. Sleep-time compute matches test-time tokens only; ACE multi-epoch (+2.6 on AppWorld) adds tokens. Also no LLM agent has been run on reward-versus-transition revaluation with an added replay step.
agent_test: Run replay-pass vs fresh-attempt arms at equal total tokens on repeated item families.
